charm.how: Complete the National Pokédex (Mythicals not needed), then talk to Professor Birch in Littleroot Town. Completing the Hoenn Pokédex gives the Oval Charm instead.

methods.name: Random encounters
methods.plain: Any Pokémon you meet has a 1 in 4,096 chance to be shiny.
methods.detail: One try at the base odds per Pokémon, 3 with the Shiny Charm. In a horde each of the 5 Pokémon rolls on its own.

methods.name: Masuda Method
methods.plain: Breed two Pokémon whose games are in different languages: the eggs have a much better shiny chance.
methods.detail: 6 tries per egg, 8 with the Shiny Charm.

methods.name: Breeding (same-language parents)
methods.plain: Ordinary eggs have the normal shiny chance; the Shiny Charm helps them too.

methods.name: Chain fishing
methods.plain: Fish in the same spot and reel something in every time: each hook in a row raises the odds, to about 1 in 100 after 20 in a row.
methods.detail: 1 try plus 2 per hook in a row, up to a chain of 20 (41 tries, 43 with the Shiny Charm). A missed bite or moving away breaks the chain.

methods.name: DexNav
methods.plain: Sneak up on Pokémon you find with the DexNav. The more of one species you find, the better its shiny odds, and the 50th and 100th in a chain get a big boost.
methods.detail: Search level points (6 per level up to 100, 2 per level up to 200, then 1 per level, all × 0.01) give a ceil(points) in 10,000 chance per check. Checks: 1, +2 with the Shiny Charm, +5 on the 50th in a chain, +10 on the 100th, +4 on a random 4% boost. If every check fails, the normal odds still apply.
methods.note: mrnbayoh's DexNav code analysis; results are rounded from it. The '+4 every 5th chain' claim is unverified and left out.
